(2) A sharp macro close-up of a single hair follicle on human skin appears, showing a red, inflamed bump with a visible hair in the center. (3) The host continues her explanation, gesturing with her hands. (4) Cut to a wide shot of an outdoor thermal hot spring in Beitou, featuring several people soaking in pools surrounded by lush green trees and steam. (5) Cut to a close-up of a luxury indoor whirlpool tub with swirling blue water and bubbles. (6) A sequence of still images shows a person's abdomen and side with widespread red rashes and pustules. (7) The host is seen again in the studio, with animated graphics of green and blue bacteria icons and a cartoon sun appearing on screen. (8) Footage of an outdoor hot spring at night shows steam rising from a pool while a person is visible in the background. (9) The host points to several animated graphics including a person in a tub and a medicine bottle. (10) The final shot is a white end screen containing the clinic logo, contact information including a Line ID, phone number, and two physical addresses in Taipei.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a public health education short by a dermatologist explaining 'Hot Tub Folliculitis.' It identifies symptoms from real-world examples, explains the cause (bacteria in public baths), provides a timeline for recovery, and encourages professional consultation if symptoms persist, while cautioning against unsanitary facilities.
